instruction.what: The evidence validation (B5) of one subgroup, after its sweep, the gate before 3.1: the code checks of its observations (shown in `code_checks`), and the reading of every evidence observation of the subgroup (its own of S1 to 2.1, and the older ones on its occurrences kept as evidence) for whether it is true, founded and coherent with the others. Inner being is not judged here; the two validations are never run together.
read: Read the code checks first: a failing check names observations to repair (unmarked, no node, a word node missing a column without its reason, a trace to a deleted observation, two of one text, a B1 observation no sense traces, a sense the 2.1 observations on its occurrences do not trace, an older observation left open).

Take one observation at a time (`observations`, in the order of the steps): its text, basis and grounds against its verses (`verses`) and the observations it traces. Is it true of those verses? Does it say more than they show? Does it contradict another observation of the subgroup?
write: Fill `answer.observations`, one entry for each observation of the package: verdict true, with `why` (what in the verses and the data bears it out); or verdict repair, with `why` (what is wrong) and `actions`: the actions of the validation that repair it (cfg_setting validate.reading actions, each with its parameters, for example {"action": "restate", "oid": id, "new_text": ..., "checked": ..., "reason": ...}, or delete_neither, complete_node, add_trace).
A repair is checked as it is written; an observation that cannot be made true is deleted with its reason.

Then: Collection-Build.ps1 -Action RecordEvidence -File <the answer file> (-Check to preview), and ReadEvidence again until every evidence observation is read; the gate passes when all are read and the code checks pass.

keep.text: A sheet of validation actions is checked whole (every action named, its parameters complete) and written in one transaction: any action the tables refuse refuses the whole sheet and nothing is kept. -Check runs every action and rolls back. Every change is kept in ib_observation_change with its reason (RW-01); nothing is physically deleted.

A finding of the validation is repaired first: a wording that is untrue or stronger than its verse is restated and the restatement checked against the base data; a node missing a column is completed, or the reason the data cannot give it is recorded; a duplicate is consolidated; a node is deleted only when another live node carries its occurrence or it supports no finding of its observation. A finding is left open only when a named collection's validation will touch the observation: the deferral to that collection and the finding are recorded, and the check accepts it as deferred. A finding with no named owner is closed in the validation.

An older observation is deleted as consumed only when live observations carry its meaning: every word occurrence of it is on a live node of a carrier or named as not carried with its reason, the mapping is stated in words (what the old says, which carrier states each part), the traces to it are re-pointed or replaced, and the consumption is kept as `consumed_by`. An observation that holds more than one finding is split first.

An observation that is neither evidence nor inner being contributes nothing to the purposes of the observations (researcher, 2026-11-22): it is commented with its reason and the word occurrences no other live observation holds, then deleted. An observation already marked, or one another observation traces, is not deleted this way.

Evidence states what the data are or show, tied to a verse. Inner being states how something works in the inner being, based on evidence, a building block of the stage 5 claims. The marker (ib_observation.nature) follows the content and purpose of the observation, never its stage (RS-04): an observation of any stage may be inner being when it traces to evidence. One that states both is split. The marker is set when the observation is created, by the item that is answered (cfg_setting layer.reading items.<item>.nature); a finding file never sets it; the validation changes it only where the content shows the item's nature does not hold.

The validation runs in two layers, never concurrently: evidence first, then inner being. The inner-being layer is judged only when the evidence layer passes (every in-scope observation marked, none without a live node, no word node missing a required column without its reason, no live trace to a deleted observation, no two of one meaning). A later evidence change reopens only the inner-being rows it touches. In the build this gate is: step 3.1 does not open before the evidence layer passes, and step 3.3 does not close before both layers pass (cfg_setting layer.reading open_gate and closing_gate).
No observation is changed except by a reading, and every change is recorded with its reason. An observation no longer supported by the verse is soft-deleted, with the reason.
One observation per finding: the same description is never written twice. Applied to another verse, word or scope it gains a node on the existing observation.
Observation text is concise and tied to this verse's content, never a restatement of the word's dictionary sense. A transliteration is never given without its gloss.
Verse references are resolved fresh at write time, never taken from the text written. Relations are recorded only on evidence.
Missing data in the base extract is named as a gap, never substituted from memory or outside knowledge.

observations.text: In 2Ch 5:11 the priests there had all consecrated themselves, not keeping to their divisions: regard is keeping to an order, present is being there; neither offers.
observations.grounds: without regard to their divisions

observations.text: In Isa 53:8 oppression is what took the servant away, and the question is who of his generation considered it: the considering is of what was done to him by oppression.
observations.grounds: By oppression and judgment he was taken away

observations.text: In 1Pe 5:12 Peter regards Silvanus as faithful and, by him, writes exhorting and declaring: the regard of the writer for the carrier stands beside the preaching of the letter.
observations.grounds: exhorting and declaring that this is the true grace

observations.text: In 1Sa 1:16 Hannah asks Eli not to regard her as a worthless woman, and in 1Sa 25:25 Abigail asks David not to regard Nabal: regarding is counting a person as worthless. In Job 37:24 God does not regard the wise in their own conceit: conceit is what he withholds regard from. In Ecc 2:11 the Preacher considered all his toil, and it was vanity.
observations.grounds: Do not regard your servant as a worthless woman

observations.text: In Heb 11:11 the one Sarah considered faithful is the one who had promised: the counting rests on the promise.
observations.grounds: since she considered him faithful who had promised

observations.text: In Luk 22:24 the disciples dispute over who among them should be counted the greatest: being regarded is the prize the dispute is about.
observations.grounds: which of them was to be regarded as the greatest

observations.text: In 1Pe 5:12 true names the grace Peter declares; regard is his counting of Silvanus as faithful: the two stand in one verse without joining.
observations.grounds: this is the true grace of God

observations.text: In Deu 33:9 the Levite who says he does not regard father and mother is the one who kept the Lord's covenant: withholding regard from kin stands with keeping. In Rom 2:26 the uncircumcised man who keeps the precepts is counted as circumcised: the keeping is the ground of the counting. In Ezr 8:29 keep and weigh are guarding the gifts and weighing them by measure.
observations.grounds: will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision

observations.text: In Heb 11:26 Moses counted the reproach of Christ above the treasures of Egypt because he looked to the reward: the counting is set by what he looked toward.
observations.grounds: for he was looking to the reward

observations.text: In Heb 11:26 the counting weighs two riches: reproach for Christ is counted greater wealth than Egypt's treasures.
observations.grounds: greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt

observations.text: In Pro 12:10 the righteous is the one whose regard reaches the life of his beast, set against the cruel mercy of the wicked: regard here is caring knowledge of another's life.
observations.grounds: Whoever is righteous has regard for the life of his beast

observations.text: In Psa 119:117 the psalmist asks to be held up and kept safe so that he may have regard for the statutes continually: being kept safe is what lets the regard last.
observations.grounds: have regard for your statutes continually

observations.text: In Isa 33:8 the absence of regard for man stands in the list with despised cities and broken covenants. In 1Ti 6:1 servants count their masters worthy of honor so that God's name is not reviled: the counting guards against reviling. In Act 28:22 regard is the link word for the sect spoken against everywhere.
observations.grounds: so that the name of God and the teaching may not be reviled

observations.text: In Judg 15:3 in regard to is the link naming the Philistines toward whom Samson will be innocent when he does them harm; serve is not in view, do is his doing of harm.
observations.grounds: I shall be innocent in regard to the Philistines

observations.text: In Isa 33:8 broken covenants stand in the same list as no regard for man: the withdrawal of regard is one of the marks of the breaking.
observations.grounds: Covenants are broken; cities are despised

observations.text: In Deu 9:27 Moses asks the Lord not to regard the people's stubbornness, wickedness and sin: not regarding is withholding the reckoning of the sin. In Eze 18:28 the wicked man considered and turned from his transgressions: considering is the start of turning from sin.
observations.grounds: Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions

observations.text: In Heb 11:19 the counting is of God as able to raise from the dead: Abraham counts on God's power.
observations.grounds: He considered that God was able

observations.text: In Gen 24:22, Jos 7:21 and Eze 5:1 weighing is the weight of what is taken: the ring and bracelets the man took, the gold bar Achan took, the balances the son of man takes. In Mat 1:20 Joseph is considering these things when the angel tells him not to fear to take Mary: the considering stands before the taking.
observations.grounds: But as he considered these things

observations.text: In Rom 4:19 Abraham's faith did not weaken when he considered his own body: considering the body as good as dead did not weaken him.
observations.grounds: He did not weaken in faith

observations.text: In Ecc 2:11 the Preacher considered all his work and toil and found it vanity and a striving after wind: the considering is a review of his toil that reaches its verdict.
observations.grounds: Then I considered all that my hands had done

observations.text: In 2Ch 6:19 Solomon asks the Lord to have regard to the prayer and plea of his servant: regard is God's turning toward the supplication, and the verse gives it with listening to the cry.
observations.grounds: have regard to the prayer of your servant

observations.text: In Pro 24:32 the watcher saw and considered the sluggard's field, set his heart on it, and received instruction: considering is the step between seeing and being taught. In Ecc 12:9 the Preacher's weighing of proverbs is part of his teaching the people knowledge. In 1Ti 6:1 servants count masters worthy of honor so that the teaching is not reviled.
observations.grounds: I looked and received instruction

observations.text: In Ecc 3:18 with regard to links the Preacher's word in his heart to the children of man, whom God is testing so that they see they are like beasts.
observations.grounds: that God is testing them

observations.text: In Job 34:27 the ones who turned aside from following God had no regard for his ways: the turning aside and the lack of regard are one fault. In Eze 18:28 the man considered and turned away from his transgressions: the considering leads the turning. In Isa 29:17 turned is Lebanon made a field, and regarded is the field counted as a forest.
observations.grounds: had no regard for any of his ways

observations.text: In Rom 2:26 the uncircumcised man who keeps the law's precepts has his uncircumcision counted as circumcision: the counting reckons a state as its opposite on the ground of keeping.
observations.grounds: keeps the precepts of the law

observations.text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 the Lord asks Satan whether he has set his heart on Job, and names Job blameless and upright: the considering is turned to a man whose uprightness the Lord states.
observations.grounds: Have you considered my servant Job

observations.text: In 2Th 3:15 the believers are told not to count the disobedient man an enemy but to warn him as a brother: how he is regarded decides how he is warned.
observations.grounds: warn him as a brother

observations.text: In Deu 33:9 the Levite who regards not father and mother is the one who observed the Lord's word: withholding regard from kin stands with watching over the word.
observations.grounds: For they observed your word

observations.text: In Deu 9:27 Moses asks the Lord not to regard the stubbornness of the people: the willful hardness is what he asks the Lord to look past.
observations.grounds: Do not regard the stubbornness of this people

observations.text: In Job 37:24 God does not regard those wise in their own conceit. In Pro 17:28 the fool who keeps silent is counted wise and intelligent. In Ecc 12:9 the wise Preacher weighs proverbs. In Isa 29:16 the potter counted as clay is the reversal of the maker, said of those who claim he has no understanding. In Isa 53:8 judgment is what took the servant away while his generation did not consider it.
observations.grounds: Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise

Weigh here is weighing silver or goods on a scale; no inner operation.
Weighing names the inner operation of pondering: the Preacher weighing and studying and arranging proverbs.
Weighing here is the weight of a ring, a cloak or hair in shekels; no inner operation.
